title: The Third Autopsy
premise: Cyrus Coldharbour, a night-shift taxi dispatcher who has spent thirty years keeping her name out of every record in the river city of Marrowgate, receives two letters the same morning: one confessing to a drowning ruled accidental in 1995, and one promising that 'the third autopsy will find what the first two buried.' The letters pull her into the orbit of the Vane family, whose patriarch is preparing an anniversary dinner celebrating both his marriage and his shipping empire—both built on the night Cyrus's sister went into the water. As Cyrus works her old contacts among drivers, coroners, and dockworkers, she discovers she was the unnamed witness whose statement was erased, and that the confessor is dying and wants the truth on the record before the family can bury it again. At the anniversary dinner, Cyrus forces the confession into the open; the patriarch's heir, not the patriarch himself, was the killer, and the dying man—the family's retired chauffeur—dies peacefully hours after the truth is finally spoken.
about_author: Ivo Halloran is the pen name of a former court stenographer who spent eleven years transcribing testimony in industrial port cities before turning to fiction. Halloran writes mysteries about people whose jobs put them one room away from other people's worst nights.

chapters.title: Two Envelopes, One Hand
chapters.summary: POV: Cyrus. On her last shift before a rare week off, dispatcher Cyrus Coldharbour finds two letters in her mailbox: a full confession to a 1995 drowning, and a second note promising 'the third autopsy.' Both are written in the same careful hand. She recognizes the address they came from: Vane House. Emotional beat: dread cracking open a carefully sealed life.

chapters.title: The Drowning File
chapters.summary: POV: Cyrus. In the newspaper archive, Cyrus rereads coverage of her sister Wren's death—ruled accidental, second autopsy inconclusive. The reporter who covered it, now retired, tells her a witness statement existed and then didn't. Emotional beat: the past refusing to stay filed.

chapters.title: Night Voices
chapters.summary: POV: Cyrus. Working her dispatch board, Cyrus quietly asks longtime drivers about the old Vane chauffeur, Ambrose Pell. One driver remembers Ambrose taking a strange call the night Wren died and driving to Cutter's Slip. Emotional beat: loyalty to the code of silence beginning to feel like complicity.

chapters.title: The Anniversary Invitation
chapters.summary: POV: Cyrus. An engraved invitation arrives at the depot—Cyrus is invited to the Vanes' thirtieth anniversary dinner, addressed in the same hand as the letters. Someone wants her in the room. Emotional beat: the hunter realizing she is also bait.

chapters.title: Ambrose Pell, Retired
chapters.summary: POV: Cyrus. She tracks Ambrose to a care home above the marina. He is frail, sharp-tongued, and admits he wrote the confession—but not the promise letter. He says he drove someone to the slip that night and has carried it for thirty years. Emotional beat: grief meeting a fellow keeper of secrets.

chapters.title: What the Chauffeur Carried
chapters.summary: POV: Ambrose (flashback). Thirty years ago, young Ambrose drove heir Julian Vane from a party to Cutter's Slip, waited, and watched him return soaked and shaking. Ordered to forget, he instead kept the car's dash log—which vanished from evidence. Emotional beat: the slow corrosion of bought silence.

chapters.title: The Second Autopsy
chapters.summary: POV: Cyrus. Cyrus finds the retired pathologist, Dr. Imogen Sarr, who performed the second autopsy under pressure. Sarr reveals the first report was altered before it reached her, and that someone from Vane Shipping paid for 'inconclusive.' Emotional beat: fury at how thoroughly money rewrites bodies.

chapters.title: Julian Vane, Golden Boy
chapters.summary: POV: Cyrus. Julian, now running the shipping line, approaches Cyrus at the depot—charming, watchful, offering her a consulting fee for 'family history research.' He knows exactly who she is. Emotional beat: the vertigo of being seen after decades of invisibility.

chapters.title: The Missing Dash Log
chapters.summary: POV: Cyrus. Following Ambrose's clue, Cyrus learns the dash log surfaced briefly in a 2001 insurance dispute and was purchased by the Vanes' lawyer, Corliss Ashe. The firm still holds it in deep archive. Emotional beat: hope with a price tag attached.

chapters.title: Tail Lights
chapters.summary: POV: Cyrus. A black sedan follows Cyrus home from the archive. She loses it using routes only a dispatcher would know, but the message is clear: stop. Her depot manager warns her someone called asking about her shifts. Emotional beat: invisibility failing as armor.

chapters.title: Wren's Last Night
chapters.summary: POV: Wren (flashback). The night of the party, Wren—a waitress at Vane House—saw something by the boathouse and told Julian she'd go to the police. She never made the call. Emotional beat: a sister restored to agency, not just victimhood.

chapters.title: Corliss Ashe's Ledger
chapters.summary: POV: Cyrus. Cyrus confronts the aging lawyer, who neither confirms nor denies but lets slip that the archive box was moved last month—at Julian's instruction. Something is being destroyed before the dinner. Emotional beat: the clock starting to run.

chapters.title: The Promise Letter's Author
chapters.summary: POV: Cyrus. Handwriting analysis via an old forger contact points not to Ambrose but to someone inside Vane House: the matriarch, Eleanor Vane, who has known for years and wants the truth served at her own table. Emotional beat: an unexpected ally with her own agenda.

chapters.title: Eleanor's Terms
chapters.summary: POV: Eleanor. Eleanor meets Cyrus in the conservatory: she will get Cyrus into the archive before the dinner, but the truth must come out publicly, at the toast—not quietly, not legally first. She wants her husband's legacy cleansed by firelight, not lawyers. Emotional beat: alliance sealed in mutual use.

chapters.title: Break-In at Deep Archive
chapters.summary: POV: Cyrus. Using a driver's delivery route as cover, Cyrus reaches the archive box—empty except for a single photocopied page Ambrose's ally left behind: the log's final entry, timestamped the hour of Wren's death. Emotional beat: triumph curdling into exposure.

chapters.title: Burn Notice
chapters.summary: POV: Cyrus. Julian fires the depot's contract with the taxi company and has Cyrus followed openly now. Ambrose suffers a 'fall' at the care home—he survives, barely. Cyrus realizes Julian will kill again rather than let the dinner happen. Emotional beat: fear sharpening into resolve.

chapters.title: The Third Autopsy
chapters.summary: POV: Dr. Sarr. Sarr, moved by conscience, privately reexamines preserved tissue slides and finds evidence consistent with restraint injuries suppressed in both prior reports. The 'third autopsy' exists now—independent of any institution. Emotional beat: science reclaiming what power buried.

chapters.title: Thirty Years of Alibis
chapters.summary: POV: Cyrus. Cyrus maps the alibi web: the father covered for the son, the lawyer shredded, the pathologist was paid, the chauffeur was threatened—and Cyrus herself was erased. Every thread leads back to one protective lie told in 1995. Emotional beat: the architecture of corruption laid bare.

chapters.title: The Eve of the Toast
chapters.summary: POV: Cyrus. On the dinner's eve, Ambrose wakes long enough to give Cyrus a sworn statement he's kept drafted for decades. Julian offers Cyrus a final bribe—her sister's case closed forever, generously funded. She declines. Emotional beat: the quiet before the breaking.

chapters.title: The Anniversary Dinner
chapters.summary: POV: Cyrus. Amid candlelight and toasts, Eleanor cues the moment: Cyrus stands and reads the dash log entry aloud as Sarr's findings circulate to seated guests—including two journalists Eleanor invited. Julian denies, then implicates his father's cover-up, then breaks. Emotional beat: the climax—truth detonating at the table built to celebrate the lie.

chapters.title: Arrests and Aftermath
chapters.summary: POV: Cyrus. Julian is charged; the elderly patriarch, complicit in the cover-up, faces justice he cannot outlive cleanly. Ambrose dies two days later, at peace, his confession finally true on the record. Sarr files the third autopsy formally. Emotional beat: justice arriving late but arriving whole.

chapters.title: Back on the Board
chapters.summary: POV: Cyrus. Weeks later, Cyrus returns to the night shift, her name now in newspapers she once avoided. She visits Wren's grave with the corrected report and takes a dispatch call from a scared stranger, patient and steady. Emotional beat: visibility chosen, grief carried forward, loyalty realigned with truth.
